| $x_2$ | **$7$** | **$6.5$** | **$6$** | **$5$** | **$3$** |
| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $5$ | $9$ | $15$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072540/assets/9da2a49a4bab645fa1b8ea3f98e6aa6135b191e121d0cc78a73b517fbc510fc0.png)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Find  $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$ in this context.
e-5614.worked_solution:
| $x_1$ | **$\color{blue}1$** | **$\color{blue}2$** | **$\color{blue}3$** | **$\color{blue}4$** | **$\color{blue}5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x_2$ | **$\color{purple}7$** | **$\color{purple}6.5$** | **$\color{purple}6$** | **$\color{purple}5$** | **$\color{purple}3$** |
| $y$ | $\color{red}1$ | $\color{red}2$ | $\color{red}5$ | $\color{red}9$ | $\color{red}15$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ 9 \\ 15\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

$$
y= \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 +\beta_3 x_3

$$

$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

Question 1
?
x1 1 2 3 4 5
x2 8 15 29 22 41
y 0 −10 −6 5 11

The vector of coefficients of the plane y=β0+β1x1+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[0−10−6511]
b
[180215−10329−6422554111]
c
[1181215132914221541]
d
[18215329422541]
e
[12345]

decision.explanation: Each observation contributes a row [1, x₁, x₂], where the leading 1 multiplies the intercept β₀. These rows give exactly option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$15$** | **$29$** | **$22$** | **$41$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $5$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$15$** | **$29$** | **$22$** | **$41$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $5$ | $11$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 15 \\ 1 & 3 & 29 \\ 1 & 4 & 22 \\ 1 & 5 & 41\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -10 \\ -6 \\ 5 \\ 11\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |

| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$15$** | **$29$** | **$22$** | **$41$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $5$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

Question 2
?
x1 1 2 3 4 5
x2 10 28 13 34 40
y 0 −2 −8 3 10

The vector of coefficients of the plane y=β0+β1x1+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[12345]
b
[110228313434540]
c
[0−2−8310]
d
[11101228131314341540]
e
[1100228−2313−8434354010]
Submit

decision.explanation: The design matrix has one row [1, x₁, x₂] per observation. The first column accounts for the intercept β₀, and the remaining columns contain the given predictor values. This is option d.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$28$** | **$13$** | **$34$** | **$40$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-8$ | $3$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$28$** | **$13$** | **$34$** | **$40$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-8$ | $3$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 1 & 2 & 28 \\ 1 & 3 & 13 \\ 1 & 4 & 34 \\ 1 & 5 & 40\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -8 \\ 3 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 2
?
x1 1 2 3 4 5
x2 10 28 13 34 40
y 0 −2 −8 3 10

The vector of coefficients of the plane y=β0+β1x1+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[12345]
b
[110228313434540]
c
[0−2−8310]
d
[11101228131314341540]
e
[1100228−2313−8434354010]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION
x1 1 2 3 4 5
x2 10 28 13 34 40
y 0 −2 −8 3 10

The coefficients of the plane

y=β0+β1x1+β2x2

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[11101228131314341540]⏞X[β0β1β2]⏞β=[0−2−8310]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d: each row is [1, x₁, x₂], including a column of ones for the intercept. The submitted option b omits that column.

content.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$28$** | **$13$** | **$34$** | **$40$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-8$ | $3$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$28$** | **$13$** | **$34$** | **$40$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-8$ | $3$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 1 & 2 & 28 \\ 1 & 3 & 13 \\ 1 & 4 & 34 \\ 1 & 5 & 40\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -8 \\ 3 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

?

x2 2 6 9 11 15
x3 −5 −1 0 3 5
y 0 4 7 9 11

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane y=β0+β1x1+β2x2+β3x3 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β0β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[112−5126−113901411315155]

[12345]

decision.explanation: Each observation gives a row [1, x₁, x₂, x₃]. The leading 1 multiplies the intercept β₀, and the other entries multiply the three predictor coefficients. Option a contains exactly these rows.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$9$** | **$11$** | **$15$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$-5$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $4$ | $7$ | $9$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$9$** | **$11$** | **$15$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$-5$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $4$ | $7$ | $9$ | $11$ |

The coefficients of the hyperplane  

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 6 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 11 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 & 15 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 7 \\ 9 \\ 11\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$9$** | **$11$** | **$15$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$-5$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$3$** | **$5$** |
| $y$ | $0$ | $4$ | $7$ | $9$ | $11$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The coefficients of the hyperplane

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[11225121761315914111315825]⏞X[β0β1β2β3]⏞β=[70−1−3−6]⏞y,

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

$$

[β0β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

[−4091221]

[18213322427535]

decision.explanation: Each row of X is [1, x₁, x₂], with 1 multiplying the intercept β₀. Using the given predictor values gives option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$13$** | **$22$** | **$27$** | **$35$** |
| $y$ | $-4$ | $0$ | $9$ | $12$ | $21$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$8$** | **$13$** | **$22$** | **$27$** | **$35$** |
| $y$ | $-4$ | $0$ | $9$ | $12$ | $21$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 13 \\ 1 & 3 & 22 \\ 1 & 4 & 27 \\ 1 & 5 & 35\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 9 \\ 12 \\ 21\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The vector of coefficients of the plane y=β1x1+β2x2 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β1β2]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[−11−461220]
b
[1−112−436412520]
c
[1725317420530]

[12345]

[117125131714201530]

decision.explanation: The model y = β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ has no intercept, so each row of X is [x₁, x₂]. The given predictor pairs form exactly option c.

after.problem:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$7$** | **$5$** | **$17$** | **$20$** | **$30$** |
| $y$ | $-11$ | $-4$ | $6$ | $12$ | $20$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $y$ | $-11$ | $-4$ | $6$ | $12$ | $20$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 \\ 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 17 \\ 4 & 20 \\ 5 & 30\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-11 \\ -4 \\ 6 \\ 12 \\ 20\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$7$** | **$5$** | **$17$** | **$20$** | **$30$** |
| $y$ | $-11$ | $-4$ | $6$ | $12$ | $20$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

[β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$20$** | **$10$** | **$5$** | **$2$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$45$** | **$54$** | **$65$** | **$77$** | **$90$** |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-4$ | $0$ | $5$ | $12$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$20$** | **$10$** | **$5$** | **$2$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | $45$ | $54$ | $65$ | $77$ | $90$ |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-4$ | $0$ | $5$ | $12$ |

The coefficients of the hyperplane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 30 & 45 \\ 2 & 20 & 54 \\ 3 & 10 & 65 \\ 4 & 5 & 77 \\ 5 & 2 & 90\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$20$** | **$10$** | **$5$** | **$2$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$45$** | **$54$** | **$65$** | **$77$** | **$90$** |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-4$ | $0$ | $5$ | $12$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

The coefficients of the hyperplane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 30 & 45 \\ 2 & 20 & 54 \\ 3 & 10 & 65 \\ 4 & 5 & 77 \\ 5 & 2 & 90\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Question 8
?
x1 1 2 3 4 5
x2 30 25 20 15 12
x3 2 6 12 20 30
y −10 −6 0 4 10

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane y=β1x1+β2x2+β3x3 that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as

[β1β2β3]=(XTX)−1XTy,

where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix X in this context?

a
[10−60410]
b
[12345]
c
[1130212256132012141520151230]
d
[11301215132014151512]
e
[13022256320124152051230]
Submit

decision.explanation: There is no intercept term, so each row of X is [x₁, x₂, x₃]. Option e contains all five predictor triples in the given order.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$25$** | **$20$** | **$15$** | **$12$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$12$** | **$20$** | **$30$** |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $0$ | $4$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$25$** | **$20$** | **$15$** | **$12$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$12$** | **$20$** | **$30$** |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $0$ | $4$ | $10$ |

The coefficients of the hyperplane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 30 & 2 \\ 2 & 25 & 6 \\ 3 & 20 & 12 \\ 4 & 15 & 20 \\ 5 & 12 & 30\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -6 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$30$** | **$25$** | **$20$** | **$15$** | **$12$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$2$** | **$6$** | **$12$** | **$20$** | **$30$** |
| $y$ | $-10$ | $-6$ | $0$ | $4$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$12$** | **$15$** | **$18$** | **$22$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$3$** | **$7$** | **$12$** |
| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$10$** | **$12$** | **$15$** | **$18$** | **$22$** |
| ${x}_{3}$ | **$-2$** | **$0$** | **$3$** | **$7$** | **$12$** |
| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |

 
The coefficients of the hyperplane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 10 & -2 \\ 2 & 12 & 0 \\ 3 & 15 & 3 \\ 4 & 18 & 7 \\ 5 & 22 & 12\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

The coefficients of the hyperplane

[110−221203153418752212]⏞X[β1β2β3]⏞β=[12468]⏞y,

The vector of coefficients of the hyperplane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}+{\beta }_{3}{x}_{3}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

after.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$0$** | **$14$** | **$-3$** | **$19$** | **$-1$** |
| $y$ | $3$ | $5$ | $13$ | $21$ | $26$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
after.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$0$** | **$14$** | **$-3$** | **$19$** | **$-1$** |
| $y$ | $3$ | $5$ | $13$ | $21$ | $26$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 14 \\ 0 & -3 \\ 1 & 19 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 13 \\ 21 \\ 26\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Elements of a Multiple Linear Regression That Passes Through the Origin
content.problem:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$0$** | **$14$** | **$-3$** | **$19$** | **$-1$** |
| $y$ | $3$ | $5$ | $13$ | $21$ | $26$ |

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using multiple linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?
content.worked_solution:
| ${x}_{1}$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${x}_{2}$ | **$0$** | **$14$** | **$-3$** | **$19$** | **$-1$** |
| $y$ | $3$ | $5$ | $13$ | $21$ | $26$ |

The coefficients of the plane 

$$
y={\beta }_{1}{x}_{1}+{\beta }_{2}{x}_{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 14 \\ 0 & -3 \\ 1 & 19 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 13 \\ 21 \\ 26\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.
